evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never delivered recognizable framing about 10–15 minute call or promise of dependable quote before launching into discovery. Jumped directly into 'I'll walk through this and then you can tell me what changes need to be made.'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked only after extensive logistics probing was already underway: 'did you have any just like top of my concerns or questions that I can kind of answer while the system's doing its thing.' This came after 10+ minutes of furniture and room-by-room detail gathering.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised concern about licensing/insurance and bad prior experience with low-budget movers. Rep followed up: 'We are... We definitely do our due diligence and then of course all of our movers are professionally trained embedded. They are not daily contract workers so it a thousand percent makes a difference in the service.' Customer then elaborated further on her concerns about mover training/professionalism, and rep engaged on that topic.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection. Rep acknowledged the concern ('Oh I'm so sorry about that') and pivoted directly to Einstein's credentials rather than reflecting back what was heard.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gave hourly rate ($200/hr for 2 movers, 26-foot truck) and estimated 8–9 hours for a total of $1,775–$1,975, personalized by mentioning the customer's prep level and specific items. Included note about customer paying only for time used.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep disclosed trip fee ($105, already included), no hidden fees, no credit card fees, and mentioned travel/taxes/insurance included. Did mention 'no worries damage coverage' covers up to $2,000 but did not explicitly frame the 2.5-hour minimum or 15-minute-increment commitment.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent. Instead transitioned immediately into explaining the estimate flexibility and time-based billing.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep mentioned 'on time guarantee' by name but did not cover the discount terms—did not explain that Einstein discounts immediately if late, only that 'we have a truck available first thing in the morning with the start time between 8:00 and 10.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full coverage delivered: 'no worries damage coverage. That is also on top of like our insurance which covers up to $2,000 for any kind of incidentals' and framed as built-in ('that's also on top of like our insurance').
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep did not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar. Instead moved directly into booking and truck availability.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Asked as 'Are there any other questions that I can answer?' — the generic throwaway version with no genuine emotional specificity.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent. Instead offered to send quote and said 'you can honestly just reply and say, okay, hey, yes, let's go ahead and book it or you could give us a call' — soft-landed without explicit ask. Customer declined booking and said she was getting other quotes.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep mentioned 'There is no deposit if you need to cancel if you need to change it if you need to modify it we don't have fees for that either' — this protects the customer's rate but does not explicitly promise the rate is locked.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep did not attempt to book at all — customer declined ('I'm still getting quotes I gotta get at least two of them'). No date/phone/arrival window/crew size/addresses confirmed for a reservation. Rep only confirmed sending an email quote.

top_strength: Chauntelle gathered exceptionally detailed logistics information across two properties (1,300 sq ft apartment with 24 fake plants, 70-inch TV, piano excluded, plus mother's 500 sq ft independent living room with 70-inch TV), asked follow-up questions to clarify furniture specifics (sectional vs. sofa, TV sizes, soil in planters), and confirmed walking distances and floor accessibility—this level of detail directly supported her estimate accuracy.
coaching_note: Chauntelle skipped the high-value Section 1 'quid pro quo' framing (the 10–15 minute time-box + promise of dependable quote + waiting for a yes), which is the single load-bearing line on the call card; without it, the customer never consented to the call structure, and the call felt like a facts-gathering session rather than a guided sales conversation—reintroduce this framing at the top of every intake call before any probing begins.
